newsitem.title: USA: Vitalink sues Grancare on noncompete pact.
newsitem.headline: Vitalink sues Grancare on noncompete pact.

text.p: Vitalink Pharmacy Services Inc said Tuesday it filed a suit against GranCare Inc to enforce a non-competition agreement, which Vitalink said was entered into four months ago.
Vitalink said the suit was filed Tuesday in Delaware Chancery Court and seeks preliminary and permanent orders blocking the proposed combination of GranCare with Living Centers of America Inc.
Living Centers, a provider of health care services to senior citizens, is proposing to acquire GranCare, a provider of specialty medical services and long-term care.
Vitalink said its complaint states that GranCare is prohibited from becoming involved directly or indirectly in the institutional pharmacy business for three years.
Living Centers has a subsidiary that is an institutional pharmacy company called American Pharmaceutical Services Inc, said Vitalink's general counsel, Robert Horner.

"The goal is to maintain our relationship with GranCare. The intent was to be able to grow with them," Horner said. "We have service agreements with the company now. Obviously if they enter into a relationship with another capitve pharmacy company, they're not going to be inclined to renew those agreements."
"The goal of this suit is to protect our current and future relationship with GranCare."
Horner said it is difficult to estimate the full dollar value of Vitalink's contractual relationship with GranCare.

Vitalink issued a statement Tuesday saying it will ask the court to conduct expedited proceedings and to hold a prompt hearing on the claims in light of GranCare's plan to close its proposed merger with Living Centers in the third quarter.
Vitalink said its majority shareholder, Manor Care Inc , which is also a party to the non-competition agreement, joined in filing the suit.
